transcript.en: I've still got loads to do for our report on nutritional food labels.
transcript.zh: 我还要为咱们的营养食品标签报告做很多工作。

transcript.en: Me too. What did you learn from doing the project about your own shopping habits?
transcript.zh: 我也是。从这个项目当中，你对自己的购物习惯有了多少了解？

transcript.en: Well, I've always had to check labels for traces of peanuts in everything I eat because of my allergy.
transcript.zh: 因为过敏，所以我每次吃东西都要检查标签上有没有含有花生的说明。

transcript.en: But beyond that I've never really been concerned enough to check how healthy a product is.
transcript.zh: 但除此之外，我从没有真正关注过一个健康的食品应该是什么样子的。

transcript.en: This project has actually taught me to read the labels much more carefully.
transcript.zh: 这个项目实际上教会我要更仔细地阅读标签。

transcript.en: I tended to believe claims on packaging like low in fat'.
transcript.zh: 我倾向于相信包装上比如“低脂肪”的说法。

transcript.en: But I now realise that the ‘healthy' yoghurt I've bought for years is full of sugar and that it's actually quite high in calories.
transcript.zh: 但我现在才意识到，我买了多年的“健康”酸奶糖分高，而且实际上它的卡路里含量还相当高。

transcript.en: Ready meals are the worst …comparing the labels on supermarket pizzas was a real eye-opener.
transcript.zh: 快餐是最糟糕的…拿超市标签相比较，你就会发现披萨的着实让人大开眼界。

transcript.en: Did you have any idea how many calories they contain?
transcript.zh: 你知道它们含有多少卡路里吗?

transcript.en: I was amazed.
transcript.zh: 我是很震惊。

transcript.en: Yes, because unless you read the label really carefully, you wouldn't know that the nutritional values given are for half a pizza.
transcript.zh: 是的，除非你非常仔细阅读标签，否则你不会知道上面所提供的营养价值是半个披萨才能够提供的。

transcript.en: When most people eat the whole pizza. Not exactly transparent is it?
transcript.zh: 当大多数人吃披萨的时候。所以这不是很透明，是吧。

transcript.en: Not at all. But I expect it won't stop you from buying pizza?
transcript.zh: 一点也不透明。但是这不会阻止你购买披萨吧？

transcript.en: Probably not, no! I thought comparing the different labelling systems used by food manufacturers was interesting.
transcript.zh: 可能不会。我认为对不同食品制造商使用的标签系统进行比较真的很有趣。

transcript.en: I think the kind of labelling system used makes a big difference.
transcript.zh: 我真的觉得标签系统的使用真的会很有用。

transcript.en: Which one did you prefer?
transcript.zh: 你更喜欢哪一种？

transcript.en: I liked the traditional daily value system best - the one which tells you what proportion of your required daily intake of each ingredient the product contains.
transcript.zh: 我更喜欢传统的每日价值体系——它会告诉你每天所需摄入的每种原料成分的比例是多少。

transcript.en: I'm not sure it's the easiest for people to use but at least you get the full story.
transcript.zh: 我不确定这对人们来说是最容易的，但至少你得到了完整全面的信息。

transcript.en: I like to know all the ingredients in a product - not just how much fat, salt and sugar they contain.
transcript.zh: 我喜欢了解一种产品的所有成分——而不仅仅是它们含有多少脂肪、盐和糖。

transcript.en: But it's good supermarkets have been making an effort to provide reliable information for customers.
transcript.zh: 只有不错的超市还在一直努力为顾客提供可靠的信息。

transcript.en: Yes. There just needs to be more consistency between labelling systems used by different supermarkets, in terms of portion sizes, etc.
transcript.zh: 是的。只是需要不同超市使用的标签系统之间能有更多的一致性，比如份量等。

transcript.en: Mmm. The labels on the different brands of chicken flavour crisps were quite revealing too, weren't they?
transcript.zh: 嗯。不同牌子的鸡肉味薯片上的标签也很能说明问题，不是吗?

transcript.en: Yeah. I don't understand how they can get away with calling them chicken flavour when they only contain artificial additives.
transcript.zh: 是的。我不明白为什么他们只添加了人工添加剂也可以把它叫做鸡肉味。

transcript.en: I know. I'd at least have expected them to contain a small percentage of real chicken.
transcript.zh: 我知道。我至少希望它们能包含一小部分真正的鸡肉。

transcript.en: Absolutely.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.en: I think having nutritional food labeling has been a good idea, don't you?
transcript.zh: 我认为营养食品标签是个好主意，不是吗?

transcript.en: I think it will change people's behaviour and stop mothers, in particular, buying the wrong things.
transcript.zh: 我认为这将改变人们的行为，特别是阻止母亲购买错误的东西。

transcript.en: But didn't that study kind of prove the opposite?
transcript.zh: 但这项研究不是证明了相反的结果吗?

transcript.en: People didn't necessarily stop buying unhealthy products.
transcript.zh: 人们并不一定会停止购买不健康的产品。

transcript.en: They only said that might be the case.
transcript.zh: 他们只说可能是这样。

transcript.en: Those findings weren't that conclusive and it was quite a small-scale study. I think more research has to be done.
transcript.zh: 但这些发现并不是决定性的，这只是一个小规模的研究。我认为还需要做更多的研究。

transcript.en: Yes, I think you're probably right.
transcript.zh: 是的，我想你可能是对的。

transcript.en: What do you think of the traffic-light system?
transcript.zh: 你觉得红绿灯系统怎么样?

transcript.en: I think supermarkets like the idea of having a colour-coded system - red, orange or green - for levels of fat, sugar and salt in a product.
transcript.zh: 我觉得超市喜欢用红色 橙色或绿色等颜色编码的系统表明产品中脂肪、糖和盐的含量。

transcript.en: But it's not been adopted universally. And not on all products.
transcript.zh: 但它并没有被普遍采用。并非所有产品都是如此。

transcript.en: Why do you suppose that is?
transcript.zh: 你认为为什么会出现这种情况？

transcript.en: Pressure from the food manufacturers.
transcript.zh: 来自食品制造商的压力。

transcript.en: Hardly surprising that some of them are opposed to flagging up how unhealthy their products are.
transcript.zh: 毫不奇怪，他们中的一些人反对指出他们的产品有多不健康。

transcript.en: I'd have thought it would have been compulsory.
transcript.zh: 我本以为这是强制性的。

transcript.en: It seems ridiculous it isn't.
transcript.zh: 这似乎很荒谬，但事实并非如此。

transcript.en: I know. And what I couldn't get over is the fact that it was brought in without enough consultation
transcript.zh: 我知道。还有一个我无法忘怀的是，这系统是在没有充分咨询的情况下被引入的——

transcript.en: a lot of experts had deep reservations about it.
transcript.zh: ——很多专家对此持保留态度。

transcript.en: That is a bit weird.
transcript.zh: 这有点奇怪。

transcript.en: I suppose there's an argument for doing the research now when consumers are familiar with this system.
transcript.zh: 我想，当消费者熟悉这个系统的时候，进行研究是有理由的。

transcript.en: Yeah, maybe.
transcript.zh: 也许吧。

transcript.en: The participants in the survey were quite positive about the traffic-light system.
transcript.zh: 参与调查的人对红绿灯系统的态度是非常积极的。

transcript.en: Mmm. But I don't think they targeted the right people.
transcript.zh: 嗯。但我不认为他们针对的是正确的人群。

transcript.en: They should have focused on people with low literacy levels because these labels are designed to be accessible to them.
transcript.zh: 他们应该关注低识字率的人，因为这些标签正是为他们设计的。

transcript.en: Yeah. But it's good to get feedback from all socio-economic groups.
transcript.zh: 是的。但从所有的社会经济群体那里得到反馈是件好事。

transcript.en: And there wasn't much variation in their responses.
transcript.zh: 他们的反应并没有存在太大差异。

transcript.en: No. But if they hadn't interviewed participants face-to-face, they could have used a much bigger sample size.
transcript.zh: 不。但是，如果他们没有面对面的采访参与者，他们本可以获得更大的样本数量。

transcript.en: I wonder why they chose that method?
transcript.zh: 我想知道他们为什么选择那种方法?

transcript.en: Dunno. How were they selected?
transcript.zh: 不知道，他们是怎么选出来的？

transcript.en: Did they volunteer or were they approached?
transcript.zh: 他们是主动参加还是调查的人主动去接近？

transcript.en: I think they volunteered.
transcript.zh: 我觉得他们是自愿的。

transcript.en: The thing that wasn't stated was how often they bought packaged food
transcript.zh: 没有说明的一点是他们购买包装食品的频率，

transcript.en: all we know is how frequently they used the supermarket.
transcript.zh: 我们只知道他们去超市的频率。
